question: What is the primary goal of psychiatric rehabilitation?

options.A: Keep patients sedated in a secure hospital ward
options.B: Isolate individuals from family stressors indefinitely
options.D: Help patients regain independence and community functioning

explanation: Psychiatric rehabilitation focuses on restoring a patient's ability to live independently and function well within society. [learn more](GNS314_U5_T6#GNS314_U5_T6_h1)

question: Why are temporary leave policies used in psychiatric care?

options.A: To reduce the workload of the hospital nursing staff
options.B: To punish patients who break institutional ward rules
options.C: To permanently discharge patients without formal planning
options.D: To test real-world coping mechanisms in a controlled manner

explanation: Temporary leaves allow patients to practice coping skills outside the hospital before committing to permanent discharge. [learn more](GNS314_U5_T6#GNS314_U5_T6_h1)

question: How long does an occasional leave typically last?

options.A: Exactly six months of continuous community stay
options.B: A minimum of one full calendar year
options.C: Permanent discharge with no return expected
options.D: From a few hours to a single weekend

explanation: Occasional leave is designed as a short-term break lasting hours or up to a weekend. [learn more](GNS314_U5_T6#GNS314_U5_T6_h2)

question: A key purpose of granting occasional leave is to...

options.A: permanently transfer patient care to relatives
options.C: prevent institutionalization and maintain family ties

explanation: Short breaks keep the patient connected to their support network and prevent the negative effects of long-term hospital stay. [learn more](GNS314_U5_T6#GNS314_U5_T6_h2)

question: What distinguishes trial leave from occasional leave?

options.A: It automatically terminates all hospital legal committal orders
options.B: It is only granted to patients who refuse medication
options.C: It takes place entirely within the locked psychiatric ward
options.D: It lasts for an extended period of weeks or months

explanation: Trial leave is an extended stay in the community to test readiness for full discharge, unlike short occasional leaves. [learn more](GNS314_U5_T6#GNS314_U5_T6_h3)

question: What is the legal status of a patient on trial leave?

options.A: The patient is completely discharged from legal custody
options.B: The patient becomes a voluntary outpatient immediately
options.C: All legal rights are suspended during the absence
options.D: The formal hospital admission status remains active

explanation: Even though the patient lives outside, their official hospital admission status remains active during trial leave in case readmission is needed. [learn more](GNS314_U5_T6#GNS314_U5_T6_h3)

question: Which clinical factor is essential before approving a patient for leave?

options.A: Complete cure of the chronic illness
options.B: Ability to pay for private hospital rooms
options.C: Employment status prior to hospital admission

explanation: Patients must be clinically stable without active psychosis to ensure safety during leave. [learn more](GNS314_U5_T6#GNS314_U5_T6_h4)

question: Why is medication adherence evaluated before granting trial leave?

options.A: To prove that the nurses have done their charting correctly
options.B: To reduce the pharmacy budget of the psychiatric facility
options.C: To ensure the patient can manage treatment outside the hospital
options.D: To test if the patient develops allergies to tablets

explanation: Reliable compliance in the ward shows the patient is likely to take their drugs correctly at home. [learn more](GNS314_U5_T6#GNS314_U5_T6_h4)

question: Who must be educated alongside the patient prior to leave?
explanation: Caregivers need proper preparation and education to support the patient safely at home. [learn more](GNS314_U5_T6#GNS314_U5_T6_h5)

question: What is a major benefit of preparing the home environment before leave?

options.A: It eliminates all future symptoms of mental illness
options.B: It lowers the likelihood of rapid hospital readmission
options.C: It transfers financial responsibility to the government
options.D: It guarantees the patient will find a high-paying job

explanation: A supportive and educated family helps manage stress and prevents relapses that lead to readmission. [learn more](GNS314_U5_T6#GNS314_U5_T6_h5)

question: What must the nurse ensure the patient has before leaving the ward?

options.A: A signed contract for permanent employment
options.C: Transportation paid for by the ministry
options.D: Keys to the main hospital pharmacy

explanation: Patients must leave with enough medication to cover the entire duration of their approved absence. [learn more](GNS314_U5_T6#GNS314_U5_T6_h6)

question: Why is a written safety plan necessary before a patient goes on leave?

options.A: To give caregivers actionable steps during an unexpected crisis
options.B: To fulfill mandatory legal paperwork for the hospital board
options.C: To replace the need for professional psychiatric follow-up
options.D: To prevent the patient from leaving the hospital grounds

explanation: A clear plan ensures everyone knows who to call or what to do if symptoms suddenly worsen. [learn more](GNS314_U5_T6#GNS314_U5_T6_h6)

question: Which professional role helps monitor patients during community leave?
explanation: Community psychiatric nurses specialize in tracking patient progress and providing support outside the hospital. [learn more](GNS314_U5_T6#GNS314_U5_T6_h7)

question: How do scheduled check-ins benefit a patient on trial leave?

options.A: They allow early detection of emerging clinical problems
options.B: They replace the need for daily medication intake
options.C: They reduce the patient's interaction with family
options.D: They prove to the court that the patient is cured

explanation: Regular contact helps nurses spot warning signs of relapse before a full crisis occurs. [learn more](GNS314_U5_T6#GNS314_U5_T6_h7)

question: What is the next clinical step after a patient successfully completes multiple occasional leaves?

options.A: Immediate transfer to a maximum security ward
options.B: Consideration for longer trial leave or formal discharge
options.C: Termination of all future outpatient follow-ups
options.D: Increase of hospital restrictions and isolation

explanation: Successful occasional leaves demonstrate readiness for extended community trials or permanent discharge. [learn more](GNS314_U5_T6#GNS314_U5_T6_h8)

question: How should a nurse view a failed leave that results in readmission?

options.A: As useful information showing areas needing more clinical work
options.B: As an administrative error by the hospital admitting team
options.C: As a total failure of the patient and their family
options.D: As proof that psychiatric rehabilitation is useless

explanation: Readmission after a leave is a learning opportunity to adjust treatment plans rather than a personal failure. [learn more](GNS314_U5_T6#GNS314_U5_T6_h8)
